Subject: Weekly sync: prioritizing reserved slots across deals — cost/latency tradeoffs

Team —

CloudScale (DEAL-4783) is asking for firm guidance this week on how many reserved slots we can commit for a 12-month term. They signaled a likely close window in early May and want predictability for budgeting. I ran the attached scenarios (capacity_scenarios_Q2.xlsx) and summarized three options:

- Option A: 80 reserved slots (high confidence, higher cost) — zero burst dependency.
- Option B: 60 reserved + 20 burst (balanced) — lower cost, small risk in peak weeks.
- Option C: 45 reserved + aggressive batching/quantization (lowest commitment) — depends on infra changes and model tradeoffs.

Asks:
- Laura: confirm feasibility of 80 vs 60 baseline for May/June given other commit windows.
- Karthik: estimate performance impact / possible quantization/packing levers that reduce slot needs (if Option C is viable).
- Marissa: ops constraints (migration windows, canary cadence) if we go with Option B or C.

I shaded a recommended path (Option B) in the spreadsheet; please add inline comments so I can pull a single proposal to send to CloudScale by end of week.

Attachments: capacity_scenarios_Q2.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks —
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Weekly sync: prioritizing reserved slots across deals — cost/latency tradeoffs

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the scenarios. Quick read-through notes:

- 80 reserved: doable only if we push some lower-priority renewals (three smaller deals) into burst for June. That will increase burst pressure during peak windows (we're already at ~75% pool utilization on Wed/Thu peak).
- 60 reserved + 20 burst: seems like the sensible compromise. We can accommodate the baseline without moving other committed deals, and burst covers expected spikes. Recommend a two-week canary (5–10 slots from pool) to validate no queuing on day-1.
- 45 reserved with infra changes: technically feasible if Karthik's packing gains materialize. We need 3–4 weeks for testing and a rollback path.

I updated the attached sheet with utilization curves for May/June and a sensitivity tab (see "utilization_by_week"). In that model, Option B keeps average p99 latency within SLA for 95% of windows; Option A buys an extra buffer but at ~18% higher monthly commitment.

Attachments: capacity_scenarios_Q2.xlsx (updated)

Laura Bennett
Director, Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly sync: prioritizing reserved slots across deals — cost/latency tradeoffs

Laura / Jordan —

Quick technical read: the numbers on the "aggressive packing" tab are reasonable. A few implementation notes:

- We can reduce slot demand by ~20–30% for CloudScale's workload by shipping two items: tighter GPU packing (smaller batch windows) and a light int8 quantization profile for the base model. Both are low-risk but need a staged rollout.
- If CloudScale insists on 80 reserved, we should still schedule the packing rollout — it will free pool capacity for other deals starting month 3.
- Fallback policy: set a hard burst cap at 25 slots and an automated fallback to a slightly smaller model variant if queue > 30s for >3 mins. That preserves p99 targets without overcommitting hardware.

From a fleet perspective, Option B + packing gives the best long-term capacity elasticity. I'll draft the runbook for the canary and the fallback automation this week.

Karthik Iyer
